questions.text: The number of states required by a Finite State Machine,to simulate the behavior of a computer with a memory capable of storing 'm' words, each of length 'n' bits is?
questions.solution:
The memory holds m [latex]\times[/latex] n bits in total. Each distinct content of the memory is a different state.

Number of states = [latex]2^{mn}[/latex]

Answer: [latex]2^{mn}[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider the following languages over the alphabet [latex]\sum =\{0,1,c\}: [/latex]
[latex]L_{1}=\{0^{n}|1^{n}|n\geq 0\}[/latex]
[latex]L_{2}=\{wcw^{r}|w\in \{0,1\}^{*}\}[/latex]
[latex] L_{3}=\{ww^{r}|w\in \{0,1\}^{*}\}[/latex]
Here [latex]w^{r}[/latex] is the reverse of the string w. Which of these languages are deterministic Contextfree languages?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]L_1=\{0^n1^n\}[/latex]: push 0s, pop on 1s [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] DCFL.
- [latex]L_2=\{wcw^r\}[/latex]: c marks the middle, so the PDA knows when to start popping [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] DCFL.
- [latex]L_3=\{ww^r\}[/latex]: the middle must be guessed [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL but not DCFL.

Answer: Only L1 and L2

questions.text: Which one of the following problems is undecidable?
questions.solution:
Membership (CYK), emptiness and finiteness of CFLs are all decidable.

Ambiguity of a CFG is undecidable (reduction from Post Correspondence Problem).

Answer: Deciding if a given context-free grammar is ambiguous

questions.text: Let [latex]\Sigma[/latex] be a finite non-empty alphabet and let [latex]2^{\Sigma^{*}}[/latex] be the power set of [latex]\Sigma^{*}[/latex] . Which one of the following is TRUE?
questions.solution:
[latex]\Sigma^*[/latex] can be listed in order of length (then dictionary order), so it is countably infinite.

[latex]2^{\Sigma^*}[/latex] is the power set of a countably infinite set, which is uncountable (Cantor's theorem).

Answer: [latex]2^{\Sigma^*}[/latex] is uncountable and [latex]\Sigma^*[/latex] is countable

questions.text:
The length of the shortest string NOT in the language (over [latex]\Sigma[/latex]={a,b}) of the following regular expression is _________.
a*b* (ba)* a*
questions.solution:
All strings of length 0, 1, 2 are generated: [latex]\epsilon[/latex], a, b, aa, ab, bb (from a*b*), ba (from (ba)*).

"bab": after the leading b's we need "ab", but "ab" cannot come from (ba)*a*. So bab is not in the language.

Answer: 3
